notes.decision: Translated 'far away in the speech of God' — circumstantial clause with ⲍⲙ̄ ('in') as instrumental/locative. The peoples are far in language and geography, yet bless Mani's name in all lands. Possibly read as 'far (yet) by the word of God' — i.e., the divine word reaches them in their distance.

Read as Coptic idiom for 'act beforehand against me' — ⲣ̄ + ⲡⲁⲧ-ⲟⲧⲟⲩ ('lay-foot/hand-against-them') with ⲛⲉⲙⲏⲓ̈ 'with me' (= 'against me' in hostile context). The kings together with magnates, orders, and powers attempted to cut Mani off from the truth but failed — Manichaean martyrological topos.

Read ⲁ̄ⲡⲉⲓ̈ as exclamatory 'Look! Behold!' and ⲉⲥⲭⲉ as Lyc. ⲉϣϫⲉ 'if/since.' The full sense: 'Look! — if then I am alone, why have they not been able against me?' The implied answer is that Jesus son of Greatness stands with him.

Lyc. ordinal ⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ 'third' (cf. ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲙ̄ⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ 'Third Ambassador'). The page presents a numbered list of Mani's distinctive achievements; matters one and two appeared on the previous page or are encompassed in lines 1-7.

Difficult form. Translated functionally as 'not one was found / could be a companion' — likely a Lyc. negative existential ⲛⲉⲩ-ⲕ̄ⲃⲛ̄ 'they were not equal/matched,' from ⲕⲱⲃ 'be paired, double.' The parallel construction in line 16 (ⲙ̄ⲡⲉ ⲟⲩⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲧ ϣⲃⲣⲟ ⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ 'no single man has been companion to me') confirms the sense.
Unidentified term, possibly 'of (the host of) Sabaoth,' or a corrupt/obscure Lyc. word. Left tentative; flagged in proposed terms.

Translated 'great psalms of Wisdom' tentatively. ⲍⲁⲗⲙⲉ likely from Greek ψαλμοί 'psalms' with Lyc. ⲍ-onset; in the context of Mani's gifts to his Sons (the Manichaean elect), 'psalms of Wisdom' fits the documented Manichaean liturgical-instructional tradition. Alternative: ⲍⲁⲗⲙⲉ from ϩⲱⲗⲙ 'image, form' (cf. Hebrew ṣelem) — 'great forms of Wisdom.'

Qualitative modifying †ⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ 'this generation.' Translated 'this latter (generation),' reading ⲭⲁⲃⲁⲁⲧ as related to ⲕⲱ 'leave behind' or ⲕⲁⲃ-ⲏⲏⲧ 'lowly, humble.' The contrast with the 'first apostles' supports a temporal-final sense ('the latter generation in which I am, contrasted with the apostolic ages of old').

Tentatively 'none of them either' — possibly ⲗ̄-ⲗⲁⲩⲉ-ⲍⲱⲥ-ⲁⲛ 'no one likewise either' or ⲗ̄ⲗⲟⲩ-ⲍⲱⲥ ⲁⲛ. Functions as emphatic negation reinforcing 'all the apostles did not do as I have done — none of them either.'
